hand-and-ball.prompt: Create a convincing synthetic monochrome radiograph depicting a real ACTION: an adult human hand in the exact instant of catching a small soft hollow rubber ball. Oblique dorsopalmar transmission projection with the five digits opening and beginning to curl naturally around the ball. Thumb on one side, four fingers staggered around the other side with distinct believable phalanges; fingertips deform the soft ball slightly. The ball is plain, low attenuation, faint rounded shell, NOT a solid dark sphere. Where finger bones overlap the ball they accumulate attenuation in the SAME exposure. The bones of hand, wrist and distal radius/ulna form one anatomically plausible continuous projection; cartilage joint spaces visible; modest faint soft tissue outline around bones rather than a skin photograph. Main wrist and palm reasonably crisp; fast distal fingertips and ball edge have subtle LOCAL motion blur suggesting the catch, not multiple intact fingers. Single grey-blue monochrome transmission image on uniform near-white detector field, HIGH transmission is light and stronger attenuation is DARK throughout. No surface studio lighting, no skin color or realistic skin texture, no specular highlights, no floor shadow, no glow, no illustrated speed lines, no diagram arrows, no medical labels or text. This is a plausible radiographic depiction of a gesture, not an optical photo of a glass hand, not a fantasy skeleton sculpture. Carefully render exactly five coherent digits with plausible joints. Sparse composition, full hand and ball inside frame. Synthetic artistic image, do not put any labels in the image.
